```plato
//==
// # Solids
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Constructive and implicit-form solids
//  - Polygon-soup solids for boundary CSG
//  - Profile-generated solids
//  - Polyhedral solids

//==
// # Constructive and implicit-form solids
//
// Solids defined by set operations rather than by a generator or a vertex list:
// the flattened constructive-solid-geometry tree and the half-space intersection
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constructive_solid_geometry). Primitive closed
// shapes (Sphere, Box3D, Cylinder, Cone, Torus...) live in the `spatial-*` files
// and serve
// directly as CSG leaves.

//==
// # Constructive solid geometry

// The Boolean operation applied at an interior CSG node
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constructive_solid_geometry). IDifference
// subtracts the right child from the left; smooth variants blend over their
// own Radius (in model units).
type CsgOperation
    = Union
    | Intersection
    | Difference
    | SmoothUnion(Radius: Number)
    | SmoothIntersection(Radius: Number)
    | SmoothDifference(Radius: Number);

// A zero-based index of a node within a CSG tree's flat node array.
// -1 means "none" (a leaf's missing children).
type CsgNodeIndex
    implements IValue, IHashable, IComparable, IIndex
{
    Value: Integer;
}

// One node of a flattened CSG tree. Interior nodes combine two children by
// Operation; leaf nodes reference a primitive by index into a primitive
// collection supplied alongside the tree. Child references are node indices
// into the same flat array, never embedded nodes.
type CsgNode3D
    = Leaf(PrimitiveIndex: ItemIndex)
    | Interior(Operation: CsgOperation, LeftChild: CsgNodeIndex, RightChild: CsgNodeIndex);

// A constructive solid geometry tree stored as a flat node array with child
// indices (no pointers); Root is the index of the root node in Nodes
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constructive_solid_geometry).
type CsgTree3D
    implements ISolid
{
    Nodes: Array<CsgNode3D>;
    Root: CsgNodeIndex;
}

//==
// # Derived and implicit-form solids

// A convex polytope given as the intersection of half-spaces
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convex_polytope). The intersection is assumed
// bounded; redundant half-spaces are permitted.
type ConvexPolytope3D
    implements IConvexSolid
{
    Boundaries: Array<HalfSpace>;
}

//==
// # Polygon-soup solids for boundary CSG
//
// The boundary-representation side of constructive solid geometry: a solid as a
// soup of outward-facing convex planar polygons, and the polygon-versus-plane
// classification the clipping and boolean bodies dispatch on. The implicit /
// tree side of CSG is the section above; the algorithm bodies live in
// `solids-csg.library.plato`.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constructive_solid_geometry)

// How a planar polygon sits relative to a plane: entirely in the plane's front
// (positive) half-space, entirely behind, lying in the plane itself (within the
// classification tolerance), or crossing it (vertices strictly on both sides).
// The four-way answer every plane-clipping and BSP construction dispatches on.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binary_space_partitioning)
type PlaneRelation3D
    = Front
    | Back
    | Coplanar
    | Spanning;

// A closed solid bounded by a soup of CONVEX planar polygons whose outward
// normals (CCW winding, CONVENTIONS.md - winding) bound a watertight volume:
// csg.js's polygon-list model of a solid. Unordered, unindexed, and permitted
// to hold T-junctions from clipping; convexity of every face is the invariant
// the Sutherland-Hodgman clipping bodies rely on.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boundary_representation)
type PolygonSoup3D
    implements ISolid, IDeformable3D
{
    Polygons: Array<Polygon3D>;
}

//==
// # Profile-generated solids
//
// Closed, bounded volumes formed by carrying a planar profile through space:
// extrude, revolve, loft, and sweep (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid_geometry).
// Each names the profile it starts from and the placement or path that carries
// it; the resulting boundary is watertight because the generator caps both ends.

//==
// # Profile-generated solids

// The solid formed by extruding a planar profile (with optional holes) along
// the placement frame's Z axis for the given Height
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extrusion). The profile lies in the frame's
// XY plane.
type ExtrudedSolid
    implements ISolid
{
    Profile: PolygonWithHoles2D;
    Placement: Frame3D;
    Height: Number;
}

// The solid swept by revolving a planar profile about an axis
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid_of_revolution). The profile's X
// coordinate is the radial distance from the axis and its Y coordinate runs
// along the axis; a partial sweep over Angles is capped by two flat faces.
type RevolvedSolid
    implements ISolid
{
    Profile: PolygonWithHoles2D;
    Axis: InfiniteLine3D;
    Angles: AngleInterval;
}

// The solid interpolating an ordered stack of planar closed cross-sections,
// capped by the first and last sections (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loft_(3D)).
// Sections must share point counts; Closed joins the last section back to the
// first into a ring instead.
type LoftedSolid
    implements ISolid, IDeformable3D
{
    Sections: Array<Polygon3D>;
    Closed: Boolean;
}

// The solid swept by carrying a planar profile (with optional holes) along a
// path in the path's rotation-minimizing frame, capped at both path ends.
type SweptSolid
    implements ISolid
{
    Profile: PolygonWithHoles2D;
    Path: ICurve3D;
}
```
